newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans fear for savings, inflation after EMU-poll.
newsitem.headline: Germans fear for savings, inflation after EMU-poll.

text.p: Most Germans fear the introduction of Europe's single currency will lead to higher inflation and reduce the worth of their savings, according to a poll published on Tuesday.

The survey of some 1,500 Germans carried out by the EMNID institute for Frankfurt-based investment broker DAVG found that 64.4 percent of respondants believed the euro, planned for introduction in 1999, would hurt their savings.
Nearly 62 percent thought Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) would lead to higher inflation.

The survey's conclusions follow numerous polls indicating German scepticism regarding EMU. According to one published last week, only 22 percent of Germans were in favour of the single currency while 52 percent were against it.
Slightly more than half of those polled in the EMNID survey said they believed non-money assets such as property or precious metals would represent better investments than cash savings following EMU.
But only 11 percent said they planned to transfer their investments to non-EMU currencies.
